lines.quote: Trump framing the high price of oil as a good thing for the United States — voters don't seem to be buying it
lines.note: reads the Trump clip (0:05) as a pitch that fails; the oil statement itself is filed to PG01

lines.quote: Republicans are pulling money from any number of their candidates — triage mode; Democrats with fewer resources see a broadening map (Jake Sherman)
lines.note: dated by report; the parties' own behaviour as the record
lines.zWhy: triage is a party that expects to lose seats

lines.quote: a great sign for Democrats — but in 2022 they lost the House by over-learning 2020, playing defense, and came three seats short
lines.note: the precedent for a miss in the other direction, dated
lines.zWhy: a lesson about under-reaching leans flip

lines.quote: growing signs Abbott himself could be in genuine trouble; Paxton's staff and fundraisers leak everything he says — ninth leaked audio
lines.note: the leak as record; 'hate him' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: a campaign that leaks is a campaign in trouble

lines.quote: Abbott is struggling but he has a lot of money; she has none — maybe one in a hundred would know her name. I didn't have time to raise money, the negative ads, and my opponent is well-funded and well-known — those are my disadvantages
lines.note: constitutive (leaked, ≈10-14): a party to the race names his three disadvantages — time, ads, the opponent's money and name

lines.quote: University of Texas — the most accurate pollster of 2024 in Texas: Talarico +3; Hinojosa +1; Railroad Commissioner +1; Lieutenant Governor +3; Attorney General +1 — all Democrats
lines.note: THE RECORD, polled: enters races.json as weight, never z; the line's z is the voice's belief

lines.quote: two-pronged: Trump is a massive drag, and candidate quality on top — all the stars seem to be aligning for the Democrats in Texas
lines.note: the frame: two vehicles

lines.quote: no scattering of polls shows her taking the lead; Abbott is up on average — but a one-in-three, one-in-four, maybe 40% chance of flipping if Democratic turnout is strong; he's won every election by at least 10 since 1998
lines.note: THE FORECASTER'S LINE: a probability stated and a prior dated (tx-gov, the adjacent seat)

lines.quote: Barbara Jordan Research Center polled Fort Bend County alone — the best indicator of suburban and statewide trends; Trump and Harris tied there in 2024; now Talarico +18, Hinojosa +11; projected statewide, within two points — and the RCP average has Talarico at about two
lines.note: the method and the number, sourced

lines.quote: a lot of this is demographic extrapolation — but if things tilt slightly the wrong way for Abbott, a Hinojosa victory too: a complete statewide sweep
lines.note: the hedge, then the sweep
lines.zWhy: the sweep is the flip and more

lines.quote: it's partly what people choose to reveal — a district moving less than expected isn't exciting; what we're hearing are the big wow factors
lines.note: selection effect named — the reader's own method guard

lines.quote: voters within two kilometers of a data center swing hard to Democrats (The Economist); data centers a huge part of the Hinojosa campaign; Sherrod Brown built his race on it
lines.note: a new object surfaces: data-center siting as an electoral issue (candidate)
lines.zWhy: an issue cutting one way leans flip

lines.quote: the single most important dynamic in this campaign: as gas prices rise, Trump's approval falls — nearly 1:1; the dip and the recovery track each other
lines.note: THE LINK: PG01's crunch as the slate's driver. The cross-arc predicate

lines.quote: he's responsible for it — if Russia invades Ukraine it's not fair to blame the president, but everyone knows it's singularly Trump causing this, and they blame him
lines.note: attribution as a frame; 'singularly'

lines.quote: AP: only 11% say Trump prioritizes people like me; majorities say his business interests and billionaires; 56% of independents say not at all
lines.note: the record, polled (weight)
lines.zWhy: the 2012 metric, pointing away from the incumbent party

lines.quote: 48% thought he was fighting for them in 2016 and 2024; his actions didn't say it — all of his policies have been focused on helping people that are wealthy
lines.note: the 2012 frame inverted onto Trump; 'all' is the vehicle — the highest-Dia line
lines.zWhy: the frame says the coalition is breaking

lines.quote: when he talks about oil prices being high as a good thing, it's a signal about the things he cares about
lines.note: reads the Trump clip as motive
lines.zWhy: motive read against him leans flip

lines.quote: what if the polls are all wrong — public and private polling both say something big is happening for Democrats; pollsters adjusted for education after 2016, for recalled vote after 2020, and missed again in 2024
lines.note: THE FALSIFIER STATED: a 2016/2020-style miss. The Atlantic as the source

lines.quote: a 2024-size miss — Democrats probably still win the Senate; a 2020 miss is the worst in history; midterms poll better; treat averages as a cloudy mirror, not an oracle
lines.note: the miss, sized; the reader's own guard on his instrument

lines.quote: off a lot for Democrats: 56–58 seats, like 2008 or 1980; off for Republicans — lose nothing and gain Michigan or Minnesota, less likely than the first; the real risk is running close in Kansas, Iowa, Nebraska and losing all of them
lines.note: the scenarios, bracketed
lines.zWhy: the bracket's centre is a flip

lines.quote: my hot take: after a decade of polarization we may be heading the other way — people hate both parties, so they're open to candidate quality; in Kansas and Texas, one-party control means dissatisfaction points one way
lines.note: the model's frame; Texas named

lines.quote: in Texas, that's why all these races are so close even though people don't really know the candidates
lines.note: the seat read as a referendum on one-party control, not on the candidate — the object's shape, stated
lines.zWhy: a referendum on the incumbents leans flip
